summary: Fire tower listed at Elsas, Algoma District, Ontario; a firelookout.ca contributor is unsure it still stands. No build history or site description found.

facts.status_note: A firelookout.ca contributor is unsure the tower is still there. A fan-site list of still-standing towers includes it at Elsas, without the asterisk used for towers whose cupola was removed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.ca gives the address as Agate, ON; the fan-site list gives Elsas. Wikipedia describes Agate and Elsas as neighbouring railway points on the same CN main line, so both names point to the same general area. The sources do not place the tower more closely than that.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: no source read gives a build date, design, height, staffing history or fate for this tower. Two web searches and the firelookout.ca record found only the contributor's uncertainty and the fan-site list entry, which is undated (it cites a 2013 MNR decision, but the Horden entry itself has no date). The Facebook group post on towers in Ontario could not be read. Location: the record's coordinates (48.55969, -83.00808) are about 9 km from the Elsas place coordinates in Wikipedia's infobox (48 deg 31 min 18 sec N, 82 deg 54 min 16 sec W), which fits the Elsas-Agate area but is not a precise match; the distance is my calculation, not a source's. The Ontario GeoHub tower layer (data/raw/ontario_lio/fire_towers.geojson) has no point near these coordinates (nearest is about 30 km away), so it was not used. The brief's record has no local_unit; Algoma District comes from the Wikipedia infobox and the story uses it as the place label. Fact-check 2026-10-20: the listing at Elsas is now cited to the fan site, the CN main line sentence quotes the full Wikipedia wording, and 'just west of Elsas' became 'west of Elsas' to match the source. No corrections proposed. Possible follow-up: Forest History Ontario and Algoma newspapers for a build year and fate.
